# PLLM

Private LLM inference documentation. Public weights; provider follows the protocol.

- [Use the Agents SDK](/docs/client/agents/): Keep the Responses endpoint and tracing inside your chosen trust boundary.
- [Chat from the terminal](/docs/client/chat/): Prepare while idle, then stream over the client-to-inference path.
- [Configure the client](/docs/client/configuration/): Separate inference, preparation, inventory, cache, and timeout settings.
- [Install the client](/docs/client/install/): Install the PLLM client from PyPI with UV.
- [Follow a response](/docs/client/lifecycle/): Commit, prepare, reserve, batch prefill, decode, and burn safely.
- [Use the OpenAI SDK](/docs/client/openai/): Point standard Responses clients at a trusted local gateway, never inference.
- [Python SDK](/docs/client/python/): Use a Responses-compatible client with automatic offline preparation.
- [Deploy with Docker](/docs/deployment/docker/): Run the three-role loopback topology and understand what it does not prove.
- [Deployment overview](/docs/deployment/overview/): Place three trust roles, route two online transports, and size inventory safely.
- [Deploy with systemd](/docs/deployment/systemd/): Install separate inference and preparation services with explicit caches and secrets.
- [Start here](/docs/): Offline prepared inventory, online masked inference, and a local Responses boundary.
- [Run your first prepared request](/docs/quickstart/): Start inference and preparation, seal an inventory, and generate locally.
- [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/): Current public-path commands, role-specific flags, and legacy boundaries.
- [Compatibility and limits](/docs/reference/compatibility/): Current implemented surfaces, validation scope, and unsupported behavior.
- [Live protocol dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboard/): Run current source end to end and interpret its observed metrics.
- [Project structure](/docs/reference/development/): Build and test the Rust core, Python runtime, and current docs independently.
- [Build and release](/docs/reference/releasing/): Use committed locks, verified native artifacts, and scoped publication permissions.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/reference/troubleshooting/): Diagnose role, inventory, timeout, transport, and checkpoint failures safely.
- [Security boundaries](/docs/security/): Protected values, visible metadata, required trust, and unsupported claims.
- [Install the services](/docs/server/install/): Install PLLM services from PyPI and validate a public checkpoint source.
- [Model support](/docs/server/models/): Separate tensor import, graph execution, public bundles, and quality evidence.
- [Rust execution core](/docs/server/native/): Maturin packaging, exact integer kernels, thread policy, and evidence limits.
- [Measure and tune](/docs/server/performance/): Separate cold inventory, compact prefill, persistent decode, and local boundaries.
- [Run both services](/docs/server/usage/): Serve a public transformer body and preload committed corrections.
- [Private inference](/research/architecture/): How model providers can execute useful inference without seeing plaintext client data.
- [Global compute market](/research/market/): How private inference can widen access to AI compute without requiring providers to see client data.
- [PLLM: Offline-Correlated Private Inference for Public-Weight Language Models](/research/paper/): A three-role private language-model runtime that prepares one-time masked matrix correlations before online inference.
- [Run your own benchmark](/research/reproduce/): Measure private inference on your hardware and extend PLLM's map of eligible compute.
- [PLLM research](/research/): The mission, protocol, and evidence for a global market in private AI compute.
- [PLLM whitepaper](/research/whitepaper/): A two-page overview of prepared private inference.
